question.text: A trader sells 10 lots of USDJPY cross-currency futures at 150.65. Settlement price is 149.85. What is the profit in JPY and approximately in INR (JPY/INR = 55.50 per 100 JPY)?

explanation.text: The Logic: USDJPY futures are quoted in JPY per USD, and contract value / P&L uses trade price x lot size in the quote currency. Profit on a short = 10 x 1000 x (150.65 - 149.85) = 10,000 x 0.80 = JPY 8,000. INR equivalent = 8,000 x (55.50 / 100) = INR 4,440. The Trap: Although the lot size is 1000 USD (base currency), the P&L accrues in JPY (quote currency); treating P&L in USD or skipping the JPY-to-INR conversion gives the wrong figures. Note: All cross-currency futures listed in India settle in INR, with JPY (or USD) P&L converted using the relevant FBIL reference rate on the settlement day.
